findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion verifying the `project.review-phase-boundaries` migration to `["**"]` (membership unchanged) and that no stale `[]`-glob-semantics references remain in documentation, examples, or config.
evidence: Body: 'Migrate `project.review-phase-boundaries` from `[]` to `["**"]` ... audit and update any documentation, examples, or config references that cite the old empty-list (`[]`) glob semantics so none remain stale'
AC only states: 'rejects an empty project code-review LLM glob list with the `["**"]` remedy' — covers editor behavior, not the config migration or doc audit
For migrations, criteria should verify BOTH removal (stale `[]` references gone) and replacement (`["**"]` in place)
findings.finding: The body requires migrating `project.review-phase-boundaries` from `[]` to `["**"]` AND auditing/updating documentation, examples, and config references that cite the old empty-list glob semantics, but no acceptance criterion verifies this migration or the doc-audit completion (removal of stale `[]` references). The glob AC only covers the editor rejecting an empty list with the `["**"]` remedy.
findings.location: Required Behavior (first bullet) vs Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: Executor migrates the config value but leaves stale `[]`-semantics docs/examples in place; no AC catches the omission at close.
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: 'The `project.review-phase-boundaries` config is migrated from `[]` to `["**"]` with unchanged membership, and a repo-wide audit confirms no documentation, example, or config reference retains the old empty-list glob semantics.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a plan-review AC/adapter behavior asserting that budget omission preserves the existing authored/default per-review cap (not the executor's generic uncapped-omission default), with a fixture/shadow check proving plan-review budget-omission behavior is unchanged.
evidence: Parent Required Behavior: 'For plan review, omission preserves the existing plan-review budget policy: the current authored/default per-review budget cap continues to apply (omission is not uncapped for plan review), so this epic changes no plan-review budget-omission behavior.'
S2 AC4: 'A positive explicit budget deterministically sheds work that does not fit; omission is uncapped and zero is rejected by the contract...' — the shared executor treats omission as uncapped.

S4 mentions 'centrality-derived default cap, explicit override semantics' in Approach but no AC asserts that omission preserves the existing plan-review per-review cap when running through the S2 kernel.
No other sibling (S3 is code-review-uncapped, S5/S6/S7 do not own plan-review budget-omission) delivers this outcome.
findings.finding: The parent's plan-review-specific budget-omission behavior ('omission is not uncapped for plan review'; the existing authored/default per-review budget cap continues to apply) is not delivered by any sibling. S4's shared executor comes from S2, whose contract states 'omission is uncapped'; S4 preserves 'centrality budget' and 'explicit override semantics' but never states that budget OMISSION on plan review must preserve the existing per-review cap rather than becoming uncapped like the shared executor default.
scenarios: A plan review is run with no authored usd_budget; because the shared S2 executor treats omission as uncapped, plan review no longer applies its existing default/authored per-review cap — silently changing plan-review budget-omission behavior the parent says must not change.
Shadow comparison (S4/S7) has no fixture asserting plan-review omission still applies the legacy cap, so the delta could pass unnoticed.
findings.suggested_fix: In S4 (cfb7), add explicit behavior and a shadow fixture: on plan review, when usd_budget is omitted the adapter supplies the existing default/authored per-review cap to the shared executor (rather than relying on the executor's uncapped-omission default), and add a negative control proving omission is not uncapped for plan review.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the post-rollback interpretation of the in-place-migrated project.review-phase-boundaries config value (rewritten from [] to ["**"]): assert that reverted pre-migration code still interprets ["**"] equivalently to its prior [] behavior, or specify a compensating-forward / value-restore step so a code revert does not leave the persisted glob value in a state the reverted code misreads.
evidence: Plan: 'Migrate project.review-phase-boundaries from [] to ["**"] without changing its current membership'

Plan Migration/Rollback: 'Keep the legacy projection non-default during the compatibility window so a code revert can restore it' and 'New code ignores legacy checkpoint envelopes, and old code ignores the new namespace' — rollback safety is asserted for checkpoint envelopes only, not for the rewritten config value
Repo fact: .rebar/criteria_routing.json line 87 currently stores applies_to: [] for project.review-phase-boundaries; the migration rewrites this persisted value in place

POST-ROLLBACK STATE overlay applies: the config change both reinterprets existing persisted glob semantics and rewrites a record in place, so the plan must assert on the state AFTER rollback, not merely that a code revert restores behavior
findings.finding: The Migration/Rollback section makes the checkpoint namespace rollback-safe (legacy and new namespaces are mutually ignored, code revert restores the legacy projection) but never asserts the post-rollback state of the in-place-rewritten config value project.review-phase-boundaries. That value is migrated from [] to ["**"] in the tracked, versioned .rebar/criteria_routing.json; after a code revert during the compatibility window the persisted value remains ["**"] while the reverted code interprets glob semantics under the old empty-list convention that the migration was explicitly retiring. The plan proves behavior rolls back via code revert but does not confirm the rewritten config value is still correctly interpreted (or is compensated) by reverted code.
findings.location: Migration and Rollback section; Required Behavior bullet ('Migrate project.review-phase-boundaries from [] to ["**"]')
scenarios: A code revert is issued during the compatibility window after the config value has already been rewritten to ["**"]; reverted code reads a value the pre-migration semantics did not expect
An operator on the reverted build re-validates or re-serializes .rebar/criteria_routing.json and encounters a value whose meaning differs between the two code versions
findings.suggested_fix: In Migration and Rollback, add an explicit rollback-state assertion for the config value analogous to the checkpoint-namespace guarantee: e.g. 'Reverted code interprets the migrated ["**"] value identically to the prior [] unconditional-fan-in behavior for project.review-phase-boundaries (confirmed by the shadow parity comparison), so no config-value restore is needed'; or, if that equivalence does not hold, specify that rollback restores the [] value alongside the code revert.

evidence: 6 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the RP-06 discovery-architecture decision (executor ownership boundaries, effective-policy snapshot, gate-owned strategy/verdict split) in a durable ADR or design-doc, not only in session logs and tickets.
evidence: 'Implement one review-discovery architecture: CriteriaSnapshot -> gate-owned strategy -> DiscoveryStagePlan -> shared executor -> DiscoveryStageResult -> gate-owned verdict policy'

'The durable intent sources are session log supporting-chummy-snake, recovery ticket irascible-clueless-basenji, and the approved decisions recorded on rubellite-secondary-cub' — these are tickets/logs, not a maintained ADR/design doc
T5e(c) asks that a novel architectural decision be captured in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update
findings.finding: The epic introduces a novel review-discovery architecture (immutable effective-policy snapshot + gate-owned strategy + shared discovery executor + gate-owned verdict policy) but commits only to transient provenance (session log supporting-chummy-snake, ticket irascible-clueless-basenji, decisions on rubellite-secondary-cub) rather than a durable ADR/design-doc capturing the decision and its boundaries.
findings.location: Outcome and Architecture / Migration and Rollback
scenarios: A future maintainer needs to understand why the executor owns budget/checkpoint but not applicability/verdict, and only finds scattered tickets
Onboarding to the policy-ownership boundary without a single authoritative design record
findings.suggested_fix: Add a child task or acceptance line to author/update an ADR (or design-doc) recording the new discovery architecture and the executor's explicit non-responsibilities (no applicability choice, no input truncation, no provider retry, no verdict).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a brief prior-art note to the Outcome/Architecture (and --retry) sections that names the established patterns the design mirrors — Semgrep/ansible-lint typed-findings-separated-from-verdict, and Nextflow/Argo/GitHub Actions/pytest content-identical resume — citing rubellite-secondary-cub, so the anti-repackaging rationale is visible from the plan itself.
evidence: Plan architecture line: 'CriteriaSnapshot -> gate-owned strategy -> DiscoveryStagePlan -> shared executor -> DiscoveryStageResult -> gate-owned verdict policy' with no cited precedent.

'--retry: reuse content-identical successes, retry only missing calls, and grant each explicit retry a fresh attempt budget' — mirrors Nextflow -resume (hash-matched reuse of successful outputs) and Argo retry/GitHub Actions rerun-on-same-SHA, per retrieved sources (docs.seqera.io task-properties; deepwiki semgrep error-handling; docs.semgrep.dev blocking-findings), but the plan does not name them.

The named source rubellite-secondary-cub records the retrieved prior art (ansible-lint 8824f98d49, Semgrep 808ee51cda, Nextflow, Argo, GitHub Actions, pytest --lf, ESLint), so the justification exists but is not visible from the plan text itself.
findings.finding: The plan crosses T1 bright-lines (expand-contract migration, a cross-invocation --retry resume feature, and a unified review-discovery pipeline) but its own text surfaces no prior-art reference or anti-repackaging note; the prior-art analysis (Semgrep/ansible-lint typed-findings-vs-verdict separation; Nextflow/Argo/GitHub Actions/pytest resume-lineage; ESLint/GitHub Actions glob selection) lives only in the cited research ticket rubellite-secondary-cub, not in the plan.
findings.location: Outcome and Architecture; Required Behavior (`rebar review-plan --retry`); Migration and Rollback
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer reading only the epic plan cannot tell whether the bespoke pipeline and --retry semantics repackage an established pattern or reinvent one.
A future maintainer evaluating whether to reuse an existing runner/resume framework lacks the plan-level rationale for building bespoke discovery/resume.
